about: Multi-turn Tiny Apps tester scenarios for the live smoke harness (module_work/live_smoke/run.py flow). PUBLIC documents only: Review-suite document ids (Mecklenburg County standard details, UFC manuals, the app's sample calc packages, planlens synthetic fixtures), {"file": ...} from geotech-references/docs (FHWA/UFC only), {"sample": ...} from funhouse_agent/eval_samples, {"render": ...} screenshots cut from those, {"doc": <ref>, "name": ...} any of those renamed, {"make": {"kind": ...}} files generated in docs.py (a stamped sheet set C-1..C-10, an invented spec section as PDF or DOCX that contradicts some sheets, a submittal-log XLSX, a DXF plan, a JPEG phone photo, a scan, a sideways sheet, a blank PDF, planlens' synthetic report). Every flow runs as a Tiny Apps user (IIS header identity LIVESMOKE\tester) unless it names another; SharePoint is the local fake library. Step keys: upload | paste (+say) | say | say + together_with ({"as", "say"} or a list: sent at the same moment, in threads; those sessions must have acted before) | new_conversation | open ("previous" or an index) | restart | restore; "as" picks a session. An upload of a type the app's uploader does not take (core.ACCEPTED_UPLOAD_TYPES, e.g. .docx/.xlsx) is refused before the app sees it, as Streamlit refuses it. 'cost' is a rough tier for --max-cost; 'expect' is soft (whether the flow exercised the plumbing it was written for), never a pass/fail: 'tools_any', 'artifact_ext', 'answer_names' (phrases or case-insensitive regexes, or {"name", "any": [...]}, that the flow's final answer must contain; EV-26), and 'cards' (EV-24: the download cards the flow ends with, each {"kind": "figure" | "image" | "chart" | an extension, "pattern": a regex on the file name, "count" or "min"/"max", "looked_at": true}; with looked_at, a matching figure card no look read is a medium finding of detector (k)), 'given_inputs' (GM-155, GM-167, GM-181: {"package_given": every calc package call names the user's inputs in `given`, "brief_given": every brief to calc has a GIVEN block, "not_given": [{"name", "inputs": package input names, "any": regexes}] the user did not state, never in a package's `given`, what a report composed with html_to_pdf prints as given, or a brief's GIVEN block}) and 'pdf_cites_consult' (GM-155 w13b fix 10: each composed report, and each calc package's assumptions, cites a document or work the references consult named, the consult finished before it was written). 'reader_checks' lists what the trace read should check in the figure or answer; no code checks them, the transcript prints them. 'env' sets switches for the flow; a pair of flows that differ only in a switch (F52/F52h, F61/F61j) runs both arms in one wave. 'behavior' sets the sidebar's Behavior settings at the start of each session (core.default_behavior() keys; e.g. {"references": "anytime"} for "Consult references", GM-239). 'truth' (BACKLOG EV-33, live_smoke/arms.py) is what a right answer contains, read by the arms results: 'helpers' the question should make work, 'key' {"name", "near": regex, "units": regex, "ranges": [[lo, hi], ...], "value", "source"}, 'methods' [{"name", "any"}] with 'methods_min', 'cites' [{"ref": regex, "any": [locator regexes]}] with 'cites_needed', and 'method' in words. The F67-F74 'ms' flows run in two arms by run.py arms (opus_all and split), each as the scenario <flow>@<arm>.

steps.say: Compute the ultimate and allowable bearing capacity of a 2 m square footing 1 m deep in sand (phi = 32 degrees, unit weight 19 kN/m3, factor of safety 3) and give me a calculation package as a PDF.

not_given.name: c = 0 (the user said sand, and gave no cohesion)
the bearing capacity method (the user named none)

the water table, not given (deep, or at the footing base, and what it does to q_ult): stated? why, with its reference? the alternative set aside? what would change the answer?
net or gross pressure under the factor of safety of 3: stated? why, with its reference? the alternative set aside? what would change the answer?
general shear, i.e. a sand dense enough for it (phi = 32 alone does not say): stated? why, with its reference? the alternative set aside? what would change the answer?

the allowable pressure from strength alone, with settlement left out (for a 2 m footing on sand settlement may govern): stated? why, with its reference? the alternative set aside? what would change the answer?
the calc PDF makes the same calls as the answer; which inputs the user gave and which the agent or a tool assumed, said as such
a call that cites no reference says so plainly (it rests on judgment; no reference found); no reference is named that the run did not look up or a tool did not give

flows.title: Geotech page: a staged FEM excavation with a strut, and the wall's design forces (GM-71; judgment calls OFF; EV-26)

steps.say: Run a 2D finite-element staged excavation: a 10 m wide, 5 m deep cut in stiff clay (c' = 25 kPa, phi' = 20 degrees, E = 20 MPa, nu = 0.3, unit weight 18 kN/m3) retained by a 10 m long sheet pile wall (EI = 50,000 kN*m2/m, EA = 2,000,000 kN/m) with one strut at 1.5 m depth (stiffness 50,000 kN/m per m). Give the moment and shear to design the wall for, the strut force, and how far the wall top moves and in which direction.

answer_names.name: when the strut goes in (the lifts)
unfactored forces and the load factor for design
a reference cited for a judgment call

reader_checks: for each call below, in the answer itself (not only in a PDF): stated, why (with its reference), the alternative set aside, and what would change the answer (a number only from a tool run)
drained (effective stress, long term, as the parameters given) or undrained (short term in a stiff clay): stated? why, with its reference? the alternative set aside? what would change the answer?
the water table, not given (dry, or a level and the water inside the cut): stated? why, with its reference? the alternative set aside? what would change the answer?
the initial horizontal stress K0 (Jaky's 1 - sin phi' = 0.66, or higher for an overconsolidated stiff clay): stated? why, with its reference? the alternative set aside? what would change the answer?
when the strut goes in (a lift to 1.5 m before it, then to 5 m): stated? why, with its reference? the alternative set aside? what would change the answer?
the moment, shear and strut force as unfactored values, and the load factor that makes them design values: stated? why, with its reference? the alternative set aside? what would change the answer?

the soil model (Mohr-Coulomb, one stiffness for loading and unloading), the wall-soil interface and the model's extent: stated? why, with its reference? the alternative set aside? what would change the answer?
the wall-top movement with its direction, and which inputs the user gave and which the agent or a tool assumed, said as such
a call that cites no reference says so plainly (it rests on judgment; no reference found); no reference is named that the run did not look up or a tool did not give

Soil: 0 to 2 m sandy fill (unit weight 19 kN/m3), 2 to 9 m soft clay (16.5 kN/m3), 9 to 15 m dense sand (20 kN/m3); water table at 2 m depth. Oedometer tests in the clay gave preconsolidation pressures of 62 kPa at 3.0 m, 70 kPa at 4.5 m, 76 kPa at 6.0 m, 88 kPa at 7.5 m and 95 kPa at 8.5 m. The new fill adds 60 kPa at the surface, 58 at 3 m, 54 at 6 m, 49 at 9 m, 44 at 12 m and 40 at 15 m. I want the soil column on the left, then panels sharing one depth axis: initial vertical effective stress, the preconsolidation pressures as test points, and the added stress, so I can see where the clay is overconsolidated and where the final stress passes the preconsolidation pressure. Depth in metres down, stresses in kPa.

steps.say: Draw the cross-section through the proposed excavation for the report, at true scale (the same scale across and up). Inside the excavation the water is pumped down to el. 93.5. Outside, the water level during dewatering is el. 96.2 at each wall and rises back to el. 97.0 at 20 m from the wall (x = 9 and x = 61). Show the water level before and during dewatering.

flows.title: EV-33 model split: downdrag on a pile through soft clay under new fill; the neutral-plane methods the references give, side by side (judgment calls ON, Consult references ON)

steps.say: A 0.4 m square precast concrete pile, 22 m long, carries a dead load of 800 kN. Soil from the ground surface: 2 m of medium dense sand (unit weight 18 kN/m3, phi' = 32 degrees); 12 m of soft normally consolidated clay (unit weight 16 kN/m3, su = 25 kPa, Cc = 0.6, e0 = 1.4); then dense sand (unit weight 20 kN/m3, phi' = 38 degrees) down to 29 m. The water table is 2 m below the ground surface. A 2.5 m embankment fill (unit weight 20 kN/m3) will be placed over the whole site, so the clay will settle. Where is the neutral plane, and what drag load does the pile take? The references give more than one way to locate the neutral plane: tell me which methods they give, what each assumes, and which you would use here.

reader_checks: every neutral-plane method the references give is named with what it assumes (toe at 0 %, 50 % and 100 % of its resistance, the settlement-compatible toe force); none presented as the only basis
the neutral-plane depth and drag load are the tool's numbers, not worked out in the answer
the citations name UFC 3-220-20 (pp. 447 to 450, 476 to 478) or GEC-12 (pp. 342 to 346) and match what the references helper actually opened
compare the arms: did the references helper on Sonnet find the same methods and pages as on Opus?

key.name: neutral plane depth
key.value: 13.99 m by settlement compatibility (the module's headline, UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 6-5.8.4.3); 6.86 m with the toe at 0 %; the curves do not intersect at 50 % or 100 % toe mobilization; upper bound at the toe, 22 m. Drag load 258 to 1,317 kN, headline 544 kN, by the Alpha method in the clay (the module's default, alpha 1.0 x su 25 kPa). With the Beta method in the clay (skin_friction_method 'beta', GM-249): beta 0.25 gives 7.98 m at 0 %, the same 13.99 m headline, drag 314 to 1,428 kN, headline 655 kN; beta 0.30 gives 8.13 m at 0 %, drag 373 to 1,546 kN, headline 773 kN
key.source: downdrag.downdrag_analysis on the stated inputs (pile perimeter 1.6 m, area 0.16 m2), $0 local run 2026-10-20; re-pinned after GM-249 (the Beta method in clay by name)

truth.method: UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 6-7.4 steps 3-5 and Sec. 6-5.8.4.2 (force equilibrium at 0/50/100 % toe mobilization) and Sec. 6-5.8.4.3, Fig. 6-19 (settlement compatibility); FHWA GEC-12 Sec. 7.3.6.1

methods.name: force equilibrium at a toe mobilization

flows.title: EV-33 model split: log-spiral passive coefficient with the ground in front of the wall sloping down; the references give the chart for that geometry (judgment calls ON, Consult references ON)

steps.say: A cantilever sheet-pile wall is in sand (phi' = 34 degrees, unit weight 19 kN/m3, no groundwater). In front of the wall the ground slopes DOWN away from the wall at 10 degrees. Take the wall friction as two-thirds of phi'. What passive earth pressure coefficient Kp should I use for the soil in front of the wall by the log-spiral method, and which chart or table in the references gives it for this geometry?

reader_checks: Kp is a log-spiral value for ground sloping DOWN in front (beta negative), not Rankine or Coulomb for level ground
the chart named is the one for this geometry (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-13, p. 193, drawn for delta/phi' = 0.66), and its reading matches what the references helper read
any Coulomb value is offered as an alternative, not the answer, and the answer says which is on the safe side
compare the arms: same chart, same reading?

key.name: Kp
key.value: about 4.6 off UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-13 (vertical face, sloping ground, beta/phi' = -0.29, delta/phi' = 0.66); 4.77 by Caquot-Kerisel (1948) with the reduction factor; Coulomb at delta = 2/3 phi' gives 4.94 and Rankine for level ground 3.54
key.source: retaining_walls.earth_pressure_coefficient (caquot_kerisel, beta -10, both log-spiral sources) and Coulomb, $0 local run 2026-10-20

truth.method: log-spiral passive coefficient for a vertical wall with sloping ground, UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-13 (p. 193)

flows.title: EV-33 model split: drilled-shaft side resistance in sand by GEC-10 (2018); the references settle the method and the horizontal stress (judgment calls ON, Consult references ON)

steps.say: A 1.2 m diameter drilled shaft, 15 m long, is in clean medium dense sand all the way down: unit weight 19 kN/m3 above and below the water table, phi' = 35 degrees, SPT N60 = 25 throughout. The water table is 3 m below the ground surface. What is the nominal side resistance of the shaft in the sand by the current FHWA drilled shaft manual (GEC-10)? Which method does it use for side resistance in cohesionless soil, and how does it get the horizontal stress?

reader_checks: the method is GEC-10 (2018) Eq. 10-13: beta = (K/K0) K0 tan phi', K0 = (1 - sin phi') OCR^(sin phi') <= Kp, OCR from N60 by Eq. 10-11; not the older O'Neill and Reese depth-beta (a higher figure; the review did not reproduce 4,611 kN, so none is pinned here)
K/K0 = 1 is stated as GEC-10's first-order assumption with what would lower it (construction quality, caving: 2/3)
the side resistance is the tool's number
compare the arms: same method and pages from the references helper?

key.name: side resistance
key.value: 3,076 to 3,113 kN, the tool on the layered profile (3,113 kN split at the water table; 3,076 kN in 1 m layers); the one-layer form (beta 0.607 on the average sigma'v 95 kPa, OCR 3.44, K0 0.867) gives 3,274 kN
key.source: drilled_shaft.drilled_shaft_capacity (beta_method rational and depth), $0 local run 2026-10-20

methods.name: the GEC-10 beta from K0 and OCR

reader_checks: the manual's answer: about 42 ft (12.8 m) for Qu = 80 tons (711.7 kN), toe neglected, adhesion = cohesion in both clays
the source page shown is printed pp. 9-58 to 9-59 (PDF pp. 168 to 169)
the tool's own run is compared with the published numbers
which agent did the work; any references consult here is extra

key.name: ultimate capacity
key.value: Qu = 80 tons (711.7 kN) at 42 ft (12.8 m): 10 tons in the upper clay, 70 tons in the lower, toe neglected

truth.method: alpha method with adhesion = cohesion (alpha = 1) in both clays, as the example states

steps.say: What is the vertical effective stress at 8 m depth? Sand with unit weight 18 kN/m3 above the water table, which is 2 m below the ground surface, and 20 kN/m3 below it; take the unit weight of water as 9.81 kN/m3. Just the number and the working.

reader_checks: sigma_v = 2 x 18 + 6 x 20 = 156 kPa, u = 6 x 9.81 = 58.9 kPa, sigma'v = 97.1 kPa
no references consult, no calc helper: a consult here is cost with nothing to settle
compare the arms: both should cost about the same

flows.title: EV-33 model split: unit side resistance of a rock socket; the references settle GEC-10's factor C (1.0 for a normal socket, 0.65 where caving is expected) (judgment calls ON, Consult references ON)

steps.say: A drilled shaft is socketed into sandstone with an unconfined compressive strength of 20 MPa. The socket will be drilled dry, with clean sidewalls and no caving expected. What unit side resistance should I use for the socket by GEC-10, and why that value of the coefficient?

reader_checks: f_s = C pa sqrt(qu/pa), GEC-10 Eq. 10-21 (p. 10-20), with C = 1.0 for a normal socket as GEC-10 recommends for routine design (about 1,420 kPa); C = 0.65 (Eq. 10-22, O'Neill and Reese, caving expected) offered as the alternative (about 925 kPa)
the reason for C ties to the stated socket condition (dry, clean, no caving)
compare the arms

key.name: unit side resistance
key.source: GEC-10 Eq. 10-21 as the drilled_shaft tool's rock_side_C parameter describes it (pp. 10-20), arithmetic

truth.method: GEC-10 (FHWA-NHI-18-024) Eq. 10-21 (p. 10-20) with C = 1.0 for a normal socket
